reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional complete real inner-product normed additive commutative group E equipped with its compatible Borel measurable structure, every measure μ on E, and every real number C, suppose that every globally C∞ function v : E → ℝ with compact support satisfies ∫_E v(x)² log(v(x)²) dμ(x) − (∫_E v(x)² dμ(x)) log(∫_E v(x)² dμ(x)) ≤ 2 C ∫_E ‖∇v(x)‖² dμ(x). Then every globally C∞ function f : E → ℝ such that f and its actual Hilbert gradient ∇f belong to L²(μ), and x ↦ f(x)² log(f(x)²) is integrable with respect to μ, satisfies ∫_E f(x)² log(f(x)²) dμ(x) − (∫_E f(x)² dμ(x)) log(∫_E f(x)² dμ(x)) ≤ 2 C ∫_E ‖∇f(x)‖² dμ(x). Here C∞ means smooth, not analytic; ∇ is the Hilbert Riesz inverse of the real Fréchet derivative; L² membership includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L² seminorm; and integrability includes almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the absolute value. Every displayed integral is the literal real Bochner integral and log is the totalized real logarithm with log(0) = 0. The compact-support premise imposes only the displayed smoothness and compact-support requirements on v, without extra L² or integrability hypotheses. C has no stipulated sign, μ is not assumed finite or a probability measure, and exactly the same C is used in the conclusion without normalizing μ.
objects: A finite-dimensional real Hilbert space E with its Borel measurable structure; a measure μ on E; a real constant C; all smooth compactly supported real functions v on E and their actual Hilbert gradients; and all smooth real functions f on E satisfying the displayed L² and integrability hypotheses, with their actual Hilbert gradients. For either g = v or g = f, the left side is the literal expression ∫ g² Real.log(g²) dμ − (∫ g² dμ) Real.log(∫ g² dμ), and the energy term is ∫ ‖gradient(g)‖² dμ.
domains: E is any type with NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace ℝ, CompleteSpace, FiniteDimensional ℝ, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. μ : Measure E is arbitrary; C ∈ ℝ is arbitrary with no assumed sign. v and f have type E → ℝ, and their gradients have type E → E. All displayed integrals are real Bochner integrals. Real.log is defined on all real numbers and has value 0 at 0. The smoothness order ∞ is C∞ and not analytic omega order.
quantifiers: Universally quantify E and its displayed structures, then μ : Measure E and C : ℝ. Assume the nested universal statement: for every v : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ v and HasCompactSupport v imply the displayed inequality for v. Under that premise, universally quantify f : E → ℝ; ContDiff ℝ ∞ f, MemLp f 2 μ, MemLp (gradient f) 2 μ, and integrability of f² Real.log(f²) imply the same inequality for f. The v quantifier is local to the premise and the f quantifier is in the consequent. There is no existential constant or additional choice of a gradient.
assumptions: The ambient space is complete, finite-dimensional over ℝ, and has the stated inner-product and compatible Borel structures. For the fixed μ and C, every globally smooth compactly supported v satisfies ∫ v² Real.log(v²) dμ − (∫ v² dμ) Real.log(∫ v² dμ) ≤ 2 C ∫ ‖gradient(v)‖² dμ; that premise has no separate L² or integrability hypotheses on v. The function f in the consequent is globally smooth; f and its literal Hilbert gradient are almost-everywhere strongly measurable with finite L² seminorm; and f² Real.log(f²) is almost-everywhere strongly measurable with finite integral of its absolute value. There is no compact-support assumption on f, no sign requirement on C, and no finite-mass or probability assumption on μ.
conclusion: Every f satisfying those four function hypotheses obeys ∫_E f(x)² Real.log(f(x)²) dμ(x) − (∫_E f(x)² dμ(x)) Real.log(∫_E f(x)² dμ(x)) ≤ 2 C ∫_E ‖gradient(f)(x)‖² dμ(x). This uses precisely the same μ and C as the compact-support premise, with no support restriction on f and no adjustment to the coefficient 2 C.
scopes: E, μ, and C are fixed across the universal compact-support premise and the consequent for every eligible f. v is bound only inside the premise; f is bound only inside the consequent. Each integration variable x is bound separately in its integral. The first logarithm is applied pointwise to the squared function; the logarithm in the subtracted term is applied to the whole scalar integral of that squared function. The gradient is the actual Hilbert Riesz inverse of the derivative of the function in question, not an arbitrary supplied vector field or selected Radon–Nikodym representative. The literal subtraction contains no hidden μ(E) factor or normalization. The cutoff definition provided in the context is not used or quantified in this proposition.
constant_dependencies: C is an arbitrary real parameter universally quantified before both the compact-support premise and the conclusion; it may be paired with the chosen E and μ, but the premise must hold with that one fixed C simultaneously for all smooth compactly supported v. The conclusion preserves that same C simultaneously for all eligible f. No new constant depending on f or v, positivity restriction on C, radius parameter, dimension factor, or measure-mass normalization is asserted. The numerical coefficient 2 and the squared powers are fixed.
